subject: Tiered fee restructure + SOW schedule sync
messages:
From: Katie Brooks <katie@auroraai.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@auroraai.com
Date: 2026-11-28 09:12 PST
Subject: Re: contract discussion — proposal for tiered fee restructure

Hi Rafael,

Thanks again for the call this morning. Our finance team asked us to propose a compact change: instead of a flat committed throughput rate we would like a tiered fee structure tied to monthly token consumption (three tiers) and a hard cap on monthly spend. That would help our board model predictability while still letting us burst for peak demos.

Can you send a draft change order showing:
- the three fee tiers with thresholds and per-token rates
- an updated SOW schedule that shifts the integration window by two weeks (we have a vendor blackout Nov 16–30)
- a note about whether we can preserve existing SLA credits if we move to a tiered structure

We hope to finish internal review this week. Attachments: none from our side yet.

Best,
Katie Brooks
Head of Finance, Aurora AI
Katie Brooks | auroraai.com

Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-28 10:03 PST

Katie —

Appreciate the clear ask. I attached a draft change order and a proposed SOW schedule that implements the two-week shift and models the three-tier fee bands. Key notes up front:
- We preserved the baseline SLA credit language — legal flagged this for compatibility with the SLA appendix but suggested a short carve that ensures credits continue to apply to the reserved capacity band.
- The tiered rates are shown both for on-demand and for reserved throughput; we included a table with blended effective rates for month 1 and month 3.
- The hard monthly spend cap can be added as an exhibit; see section 4.2 of the draft.

Attachments: [Attachment: AUR_OrderForm_v2.pdf (pdf)], [Attachment: SOW-Implementation-Timeline.xlsx (xlsx)]

If this looks directionally correct we can loop in Legal (laura) for redlines and Karthik to confirm commercial framing. I copied both.

Thanks,

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Cc: Katie Brooks <katie@auroraai.com>, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-29 08:21 PST
Subject: RE: contract discussion — draft redlines attached

Team —

I reviewed the attached change order and drafted a short redline set focused on three items: 1) SLA credit carryover (we propose language that preserves credits for reserved-tier incidents but limits aggregation across tiers), 2) monthly spend cap exhibit (we added a mechanism for temporary overages with a notification / approval path to avoid hard denial of calls), and 3) data residency/security schedule references (Aurora asked about this — see below).

I attached my redlines: redlines_AUR_MSA_rlaura.docx. High-level comments inline:
- Section 2.1 (fee bands): clarify how rounding occurs for partial-token billing at boundaries; we propose rounding to nearest 1k tokens to avoid microbilling disputes.
- Section 4.2 (cap): add an exception path for emergency product-in-demo bursts where Aurora can request a one-time uplift with retrospective billing and an approval window of 48 hours.
- SOW schedule: the two-week shift is fine but we recommend adding a contingency week for customer-driven delays (standard clause).

I will not send to procurement until we confirm whether Aurora wants the monthly cap to be a hard contractual cap or a commercial parameter documented in an exhibit. Rafael, if you prefer, we can prepare two versions for their procurement to choose from.

Laura Bennett
Deputy General Counsel | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Katie Brooks <katie@auroraai.com>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-30 11:05 PST
Subject: Re: contract discussion — tiered fee restructure + SOW schedule sync

Katie —

Laura and I discussed and we can do this two-track to move faster:
1) Commercial change order (attached earlier) with the tier bands, spending exhibit flagged as "choice A: hard cap" vs "choice B: capped-exhibit-with-overage-process."
2) Legal redline package (from Laura) that explains the behavioral difference for procurement.

Karthik will follow up separately with a short note on crediting / effective rate so you can show the board projected month-on-month numbers (we included a blended-rate table in the spreadsheet).

Next steps I suggest: 1) let us know which cap approach you prefer; 2) confirm acceptance of the two-week SOW shift + one-week contingency; 3) if you want the emergency uplift flow, say so and we'll bake it into the Exhibit and the implementation runbook.

If you're ok with either cap option we can prep DocuSign and try to get signatures by next Thursday (Dec 3).

Cheers,
Rafael

Rafael / Laura / Karthik —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. Procurement prefers Choice B (cap with overage process) — they want an approval/notification flow instead of an absolute hard stop. They also asked a couple legal clarifications:
- Will the SLA credit carve apply retroactively to incidents during a transition month when tier boundaries change?
- We need a short appendix on how token accounting handles system-level echoes / monitoring tokens; does Redwood provide a reconciled usage report?

On timing: we accept the two-week shift and the one-week contingency. Please include the emergency uplift flow. If you can incorporate Laura's suggested rounding language and the overage notification path, procurement is ok with DocuSign once redlines are incorporated.

Katie
